For this reason, use them only when they support a user need.
Link to a different site only if essential
Use them only when they are an essential part of the user journey.
Include external links when the user needs:
to complete their task on an external website
to access original, authoritative information that’s provided by another government agency or external source.
Minimise the number of links where you can.
Add in-page links only if they help the user navigate
tables of contents
back-to-top links.

rules.quote: Link to something only if it helps meet the user’s need
rules.specification: Assessment requires the intended user needs and journey. The page does not supply an independent threshold for usefulness or necessity.
rules.violation_condition: A link adds no benefit to an identified user task or navigation need, duplicates another link without adding user benefit, or leads to an external site that is not essential to the user journey.
when: External links must be an essential part of the user journey.
External links are appropriate when users need to complete a task on another website or access original, authoritative information from another source.
In-page links must help navigation; tables of contents and back-to-top links are examples.
Minimise links that add no further user benefit.
rules.why: G-2 consolidates relevance conditions for different link types rather than flagging the same unnecessary link under several rules.

covers.quote: Use images for links only if they meet a user need.

rules.quote: Use text for links in most cases.
rules.specification: Treat text as the default link medium, with a user-driven reason needed for an image link. Do not turn 'most cases' into a numerical quota.
rules.violation_condition: An image is used as a link where text would meet the need and there is no user need for using the image.
when: An image link is permitted when using the image meets a user need.
rules.why: G-2 and G-3 keep the image-link condition with the preference it qualifies.

rules.quote: Avoid implying endorsement to commercial websites in external links.
rules.violation_condition: The wording of an external link implies government endorsement of a commercial website.
when: Applies to external links to commercial websites.
rules.why: This is a distinct property of the wording, not the G-5 instruction to consult an agency policy.

covers.quote: If it does, link to it rather than duplicating it.

rules.quote: Link to sources instead of duplicating them
rules.specification: Assessment requires access to the existing information. The page gives no threshold for when similar information amounts to duplication.
rules.violation_condition: Content duplicates information already available from an existing source instead of linking to that source.
when: Applies when similar information already exists.
rules.why: G-4 consolidates the heading and its restatement; G-5 excludes the instruction to research existing content.

rules.quote: Link directly to the specific page that the user needs to go to, not the homepage.
rules.violation_condition: A link leads to a site's homepage rather than the specific page the user needs.
when: Applies when the user needs a specific page rather than the homepage itself.
rules.why: This checks the specificity of a link destination, independently of duplicated content.

rules.quote: If a full HTML version of the file is not available, link to a summary page if it exists.
rules.violation_condition: A file is linked directly without directing users to its available summary page when no full HTML version exists.
when: No full HTML version of the file is available.
A summary page exists.
rules.why: G-2 retains both availability conditions; the separate instruction about publishing format is not a text rule.

covers.quote: Give users the information they need to decide whether to download the file by providing the:
document title (not the file name)
the file type
the file size in kilobytes (kB) or megabytes (MB).
Include all this information in the link text, but remember that this adds extra information for all users.

Digital Transformation Agency Annual Report 2019–20
[PDF 1.98 MB]

rules.quote: Include document title, file type and size when linking to files
rules.violation_condition: A non-HTML file link lacks the document title, file type, or file size in kB or MB within its link text, or substitutes the file name for the document title.
when: Applies to links to non-HTML documents and files.
All the required information belongs in the link text.
rules.why: G-2 and G-4 keep the required file-link information and its placement together as one completeness check.

covers.quote: Write link text that is accurate and accessible.
If you do use images, accurately describe the link with alt text.
Don’t describe the image itself.
For these reasons, links need to make sense when read out of the context of surrounding content.
Write link text that describes the destination in clear language.
Match the content on the linked page so the user knows they have reached the right place.
Write link text that makes the destination and purpose of the link clear.
All users must be able to understand the purpose of a link without extra context.

rules.quote: Write link text that makes the destination clear
rules.violation_condition: A link's text does not identify its destination and purpose without surrounding content, does not match the linked page, or describes a linked image instead of the link destination.
when: Assess whether the link makes sense independently of surrounding content.
For an image link, assess the alternative text as the link description.
The accessibility fundamentals explicitly require users to understand link purpose without extra context.
rules.why: G-2 and G-4 consolidate destination clarity, standalone meaning and the image-link case; the explicit accessibility 'must' sets the modality.

rules.quote: Make it clear in your text that the link is external and explain why you have included it.
rules.violation_condition: Text accompanying an external link does not make its external destination clear or explain why the link is included.
when: Applies to links from the website to an external website.
rules.why: This is an instruction about words, separate from the non-text prohibition on exit modals.

rules.quote: Include keywords at the start of links
rules.specification: Identifying the most important words depends on the link's topic and the user's task. The page gives no fixed word-position cutoff.
rules.violation_condition: A link delays its most important topic or task words until after less important wording.
rules.why: G-4 consolidates the frontloading instruction; concision is a separate check.

covers.quote: Keep them concise
Use concise keywords for call-to-action text or buttons.

rules.quote: Only link the keywords.
rules.specification: Assess the clickable text or button label, not surrounding prose. Flag dispensable lead-ins and wording that adds no task, topic or action information, while retaining words needed for an intelligible label. The manual supplies no numerical word limit.
rules.violation_condition: A link or call-to-action label contains dispensable wording rather than concise task, topic or action keywords.
when: Applies to link text and call-to-action text or buttons.
rules.why: G-2 consolidates the same concision check for links and calls to action; G-4 avoids a second rule for the restatement.

rules.quote: Write links that are about a single idea, to help people to decide whether to click.
rules.specification: Treat related details of one topic or task as one idea; flag independently actionable topics or tasks combined in one link.
rules.violation_condition: One link combines independently distinct topics or tasks rather than expressing a single idea.
rules.why: A link can be concise but still combine ideas, so this is separate from the keyword-only check.

covers.quote: Put most links at the end of sentences

parts.quote: You need to fill out the application form to find out if you are eligible for a payment.

rules.quote: If it’s important for users to understand all your content, put links at the end of sentences.
rules.specification: The check requires knowing whether users need to read all the content before leaving. The manual does not make end placement unconditional.
rules.violation_condition: A link appears before the end of a sentence whose full content users need to understand before following it.
when: Applies when it is important for users to understand all the content before following the link.
rules.why: G-4 selects the body wording because it states the condition that limits the heading.

rules.quote: Accurately describe what will happen next.
rules.violation_condition: Call-to-action text or a button label gives an inaccurate or indeterminate account of what activating it will do next.
when: Applies to call-to-action text and buttons.
rules.why: G-4 uses the body sentence for the action-outcome check; shortness is absorbed into the shared concision rule.

rules.violation_condition: An email link displays something other than the email address, such as a person's name or an address prefixed with 'mailto:'.
when: Applies to links to email addresses.
The mailto: prefix belongs in the URL, not the displayed link text.
rules.why: G-2 and G-4 consolidate incorrect email-link labels, including a displayed mailto: prefix.

rules.quote: In all cases, give users contextual information in the link to explain why a link will open in a new window or tab.
rules.violation_condition: A link that opens a new window or tab lacks contextual information in its link text explaining that behaviour and why it occurs.
when: Applies whenever a link opens in a new window or tab.
rules.why: This checks required wording, not the separate browser-window setting.

covers.quote: Create internal links that support the user’s journey
Use them to help users:
orient themselves when using your digital product or service
move sequentially through a step-by-step task
find information that’s directly related to a topic.

rules.quote: Build internal links to help users move through each stage of the user journey.
rules.specification: Assessment requires the intended user journey and the site's available pages. Do not infer a required link solely because related words occur.
rules.violation_condition: Content lacks internal links needed for users to orient themselves, progress through a step-by-step task or reach directly related information.
when: Applies to navigation between pages on the same website.
Consider orientation, sequential task steps and directly related information.
rules.why: G-1 leaves the grouping heading unmarked; G-2 keeps the navigation purposes together. Missing navigation support differs from including an unnecessary link.

rules.quote: Use the same homepage links across the site
rules.specification: Interpret 'same homepage links' as consistent linked controls and homepage destinations across site pages. An isolated page cannot establish a cross-site inconsistency.
rules.violation_condition: Pages on the same website provide inconsistent homepage-link controls or destinations.
when: Requires comparison of pages on the same website.
rules.why: Consistency across pages is a different finding from a missing homepage link on one page.

rules.quote: You must include a homepage link in your main navigation.

rules.why: The explicit 'must' creates a required navigation-content check, separate from consistency.

anchor.quote: If a full HTML version of the file is not available, link to a summary page if it exists.

tags.violation_condition: A file is linked directly without directing users to its available summary page when no full HTML version exists.

when: No full HTML version of the file is available.
A summary page exists.
rules.why: G-2 retains both availability conditions; the separate instruction about publishing format is not a text rule.

anchor.quote: Include document title, file type and size when linking to files

covers.quote: Give users the information they need to decide whether to download the file by providing the:
document title (not the file name)
the file type
the file size in kilobytes (kB) or megabytes (MB).
Include all this information in the link text, but remember that this adds extra information for all users.

examples.note: The extracted example splits one sentence across blocks; these parts belong together.

parts.quote: You can read more about our financial position in the
Digital Transformation Agency Annual Report 2019–20
[PDF 1.98 MB]

tags.violation_condition: A non-HTML file link lacks the document title, file type, or file size in kB or MB within its link text, or substitutes the file name for the document title.

when: Applies to links to non-HTML documents and files.
All the required information belongs in the link text.
rules.why: G-2 and G-4 keep the required file-link information and its placement together as one completeness check.

anchor.quote: Write link text that makes the destination clear

covers.quote: Write link text that is accurate and accessible.

covers.prefix: only if they meet a user need.
covers.quote: If you do use images, accurately describe the link with alt text.

covers.prefix: escribe the link with alt text.
covers.quote: Don’t describe the image itself.
For these reasons, links need to make sense when read out of the context of surrounding content.
Write link text that describes the destination in clear language.
covers.suffix: Match the content on the linked

covers.quote: Match the content on the linked page so the user knows they have reached the right place.
Write link text that makes the destination and purpose of the link clear.
All users must be able to understand the purpose of a link without extra context.

examples.note: The source extraction does not preserve which words are linked.

parts.quote: Find out more about our upcoming events on our Eventbrite page.

examples.note: The source extraction does not preserve which words are linked.

parts.quote: Click here to find out about our upcoming meetups.

tags.violation_condition: A link's text does not identify its destination and purpose without surrounding content, does not match the linked page, or describes a linked image instead of the link destination.

when: Assess whether the link makes sense independently of surrounding content.
For an image link, assess the alternative text as the link description.
The accessibility fundamentals explicitly require users to understand link purpose without extra context.
rules.why: G-2 and G-4 consolidate destination clarity, standalone meaning and the image-link case; the explicit accessibility 'must' sets the modality.

anchor.prefix: e when they use external links.
anchor.quote: Make it clear in your text that the link is external and explain why you have included it.
anchor.suffix: These pop-ups interrupt users,

tags.violation_condition: Text accompanying an external link does not make its external destination clear or explain why the link is included.

when: Applies to links from the website to an external website.
rules.why: This is an instruction about words, separate from the non-text prohibition on exit modals.

anchor.quote: Include keywords at the start of links

covers.prefix: d the first few words of links.
covers.quote: Keep them concise and put the most important words at the start of the link.

examples.note: The source extraction does not preserve which words are linked.

parts.quote: Attend next month’s Brisbane workshop for developers and writers.

examples.note: The source extraction does not preserve which words are linked.

parts.quote: Attend a Brisbane workshop for developers and writers next month.

tags.specification: Identifying the most important words depends on the link's topic and the user's task. The page gives no fixed word-position cutoff.
tags.violation_condition: A link delays its most important topic or task words until after less important wording.

rules.why: G-4 consolidates the frontloading instruction; concision is a separate check.

covers.quote: Use concise keywords for call-to-action text or buttons.

tags.specification: Assess the clickable text or button label, not surrounding prose. Flag dispensable lead-ins and wording that adds no task, topic or action information, while retaining words needed for an intelligible label. The manual supplies no numerical word limit.
tags.violation_condition: A link or call-to-action label contains dispensable wording rather than concise task, topic or action keywords.

when: Applies to link text and call-to-action text or buttons.
rules.why: G-2 consolidates the same concision check for links and calls to action; G-4 avoids a second rule for the restatement.

anchor.quote: Write links that are about a single idea, to help people to decide whether to click.
anchor.suffix: Only link the keywords.

tags.specification: Treat related details of one topic or task as one idea; flag independently actionable topics or tasks combined in one link.
tags.violation_condition: One link combines independently distinct topics or tasks rather than expressing a single idea.

rules.why: A link can be concise but still combine ideas, so this is separate from the keyword-only check.

anchor.quote: If it’s important for users to understand all your content, put links at the end of sentences.

covers.quote: Put most links at the end of sentences

examples.note: The source extraction does not preserve which words are linked.

parts.quote: Find out your eligibility for a payment by filling out the application form.

examples.note: The source extraction does not preserve which words are linked.

parts.quote: You need to fill out the application form to find out if you are eligible for a payment.

tags.specification: The check requires knowing whether users need to read all the content before leaving. The manual does not make end placement unconditional.
tags.violation_condition: A link appears before the end of a sentence whose full content users need to understand before following it.

when: Applies when it is important for users to understand all the content before following the link.
rules.why: G-4 selects the body wording because it states the condition that limits the heading.

anchor.quote: Accurately describe what will happen next.

covers.quote: Write short calls to action that explain what they do

parts.quote: Start your application
Click here to apply

tags.violation_condition: Call-to-action text or a button label gives an inaccurate or indeterminate account of what activating it will do next.

when: Applies to call-to-action text and buttons.
rules.why: G-4 uses the body sentence for the action-outcome check; shortness is absorbed into the shared concision rule.

anchor.quote: To link to an email address, use the email address as the link text so it’s not mistaken for a website address.

covers.quote: Link email addresses not names
Use the mailto: prefix in the URL but not in the link text.

parts.quote: belinda.bloggs@dta.gov.au
Belinda Bloggs

tags.violation_condition: An email link displays something other than the email address, such as a person's name or an address prefixed with 'mailto:'.

when: Applies to links to email addresses.
The mailto: prefix belongs in the URL, not the displayed link text.
rules.why: G-2 and G-4 consolidate incorrect email-link labels, including a displayed mailto: prefix.

anchor.quote: In all cases, give users contextual information in the link to explain why a link will open in a new window or tab.

tags.violation_condition: A link that opens a new window or tab lacks contextual information in its link text explaining that behaviour and why it occurs.

when: Applies whenever a link opens in a new window or tab.
rules.why: This checks required wording, not the separate browser-window setting.

anchor.quote: Build internal links to help users move through each stage of the user journey.
anchor.suffix: Use them to help users:

covers.quote: Create internal links that support the user’s journey

covers.prefix: each stage of the user journey.
covers.quote: Use them to help users:
orient themselves when using your digital product or service
move sequentially through a step-by-step task
find information that’s directly related to a topic.

tags.specification: Assessment requires the intended user journey and the site's available pages. Do not infer a required link solely because related words occur.
tags.violation_condition: Content lacks internal links needed for users to orient themselves, progress through a step-by-step task or reach directly related information.

when: Applies to navigation between pages on the same website.
Consider orientation, sequential task steps and directly related information.
rules.why: G-1 leaves the grouping heading unmarked; G-2 keeps the navigation purposes together. Missing navigation support differs from including an unnecessary link.

anchor.quote: Use the same homepage links across the site

tags.specification: Interpret 'same homepage links' as consistent linked controls and homepage destinations across site pages. An isolated page cannot establish a cross-site inconsistency.
tags.violation_condition: Pages on the same website provide inconsistent homepage-link controls or destinations.

when: Requires comparison of pages on the same website.
rules.why: Consistency across pages is a different finding from a missing homepage link on one page.

when: Applies to the website's main navigation.
rules.why: The explicit 'must' creates a required navigation-content check, separate from consistency.

anchor.suffix: and the Commonwealth Coat of Ar

tags.violation_condition: The agency name or site title is not linked to the homepage.
